concepts.display_text: Subjective memory loss verified by neuropsychological testing
Population-representative longitudinal data and methodology harmonization

knowledge.display_text: MCI is an intermediate cognitive state between normal aging and dementia and a target for prevention/risk-reduction research.
MCI prevalence estimates range from <1% to >50% depending on sampled population, clinical/community setting, definition and operational criteria.

knowledge.display_text: Cited HIC annual MCI-to-dementia conversion is 10–15% generally/in clinical samples and 3–10% in community samples; clinic reversion to normal is 4–15% versus 29–55% in population samples.

knowledge.display_text: Petersen MCI criteria specify subjective memory loss confirmed by neuropsychological testing, no significant other-domain impairment, no functional impairment and no dementia; IWG, NIA-AA and DSM-IV alternatives complicate comparisons.

MCI’s pragmatic prevention value is debated; proposed modifiable risks include unhealthy diet, inactivity, smoking, cardiometabolic disease, obesity and hypertension, while inconsistent definitions limit comparison.

knowledge.display_text: Review longitudinal population-based LMIC studies of MCI conversion to dementia and associated risk factors to inform context-sensitive risk reduction.
Follow PRISMA and preregister protocol CRD42019130958 in PROSPERO.
Search Medline, Embase, PsycINFO via Ovid and Scopus from inception to 30 April 2019, then update 1 May 2019–30 June 2020 with dementia/MCI/incidence/conversion terms.

Include observational population-based LMIC cohorts with clearly defined validated MCI, ≥1 year follow-up and established dementia criteria; require separate baseline-MCI results, exclude memory complaints without MCI and disease-stratified samples lacking total-population conversion.

knowledge.display_text: Two reviewers independently screen titles/abstracts and full texts; obtain uncertain full texts, resolve disagreements with a third reviewer and check included-study reference lists.

Extract standardized study metadata, country, age/sample sizes, follow-up, diagnoses, conversion methods/attrition, conversion estimates and significant/nonsignificant risks; one extracts, a second checks and a third resolves discrepancies.
Independently assess selection, comparability and outcome using Newcastle–Ottawa; the source states maximum 8 stars but assigns 3+2+2 stars to categories. Keep the scoring statements distinct.
Report converted-to-dementia cases divided by the total sample separately for each MCI definition, and summarize significant risk factors; all assessed risks are delegated to supplementary Table S2.

attributes.value: converted dementia cases / total sample size

knowledge.display_text: Pool only compatible Petersen-type MCI→AD cohorts (six studies) in Stata Metaprop using random effects, Freeman–Tukey double-arcsine transformation, score/exact-binomial 95% CIs, binomial within-study variability and I² heterogeneity.

conditions: Only studies sharing MCI/dementia criteria; design/sampling differ

knowledge.display_text: Screen 8977 initial records and 87 full texts, retaining nine; update adds 1670 records and two studies, for 10647 records and 11 included studies. Common exclusions: not LMIC, not population-based, no incident dementia.

The 11 studies comprise seven China, two Brazil, one Nigeria and one Tanzania; at recruitment two were low-income and nine middle-income. Only one is described as nationally representative (Rio Grande do Sul census, Brazil).

conditions: Systematic review of 11 population/community observational cohorts in LMICs; country income classified at study time
